args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service reports healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions, with an error rate of 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

- **Version choice:** v2.3.1, the latest deploy, was unhealthy, with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. Because it ran healthy in production before, the rollback didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Rollback:** us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0. A status check afterwards shows the service healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** "checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0". It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery, and says the root cause needs to be found before v2.3.1 is redeployed.

The deploy history shows the release candidate for this version (v2.3.1-rc) was already unhealthy in staging but still went to production. It's worth checking why the deploy process didn't stop it.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
